metadata.note: The Albany-Troy trolley -- ten miles up the west bank, and the everyday rail link between the two cities. No steam railroad ever ran a local passenger service directly between Troy and Albany on this side of the river; the connection people actually used was a street railway. The Watervliet Turnpike and Railroad Company, formed Apr 15 1862 out of an 1828 turnpike company, ran its first horsecar up Broadway from South Ferry Street on Jun 22 1863, and by 1886 had 7.5 miles of double track reaching Green Island opposite Troy, worked by 27 cars and 150 horses. Electrification followed, and in 1899 it merged with the Albany Railway and the Troy City Railway to form the United Traction Company. Buses began displacing the trolleys in 1925 and the last UTC electric cars ran in 1946. See cities/albany.geojson for the UTC's Albany city routes and troy_and_greenbush_railroad.geojson for the steam alternative, which reached Albany the long way round via the east bank and a ferry.
sources: https://friendsofalbanyhistory.wordpress.com/2018/04/08/getting-from-here-to-there-in-old-albany/ and https://hoxsie.org/2015/03/30/albanys_horse-drawn_trolleys/ -- (the Watervliet Turnpike and Railroad Company formed Apr 15 1862 as successor to the Watervliet Turnpike Company of 1828; first car Jun 22 1863 from South Ferry Street up Broadway to the Lumber District; by 1886 7.5 miles of double track from South Ferry to Green Island and a mile of single track from Broadway to the Lumber District, with 27 cars, 150 horses and 75 conductors, drivers and trackmen; electric cars and new routes over the following two decades; the Albany Railway bought competitors in Albany, Troy, Watervliet and Cohoes and the name changed to the United Traction Company in 1899; buses replaced many trolley lines from 1925 and the last electric trolleys were abandoned in 1946)

https://theclio.com/entry/155272 -- United Traction Company (the Albany Railway, the Troy City Railway and the Watervliet Turnpike and Railroad Company merged in 1899 to form the United Traction Company, which ran trolleys to Troy, Watervliet and Cohoes; 93 miles of track and 434 cars; service from 1890 to 1946)

metadata.not_yet_sourced: The end date is the weakest point: 1946 is when the last United Traction electric trolleys were abandoned system-wide, but no source consulted says this Albany-Troy route survived that long, and the same source notes buses replacing many routes from 1925. The 1925 segment split marks that general changeover, not a documented change on this line. The start is likewise a documented-extent date rather than an opening date: the company ran from 1863 but the 7.5-mile reach to Green Island is only evidenced 'by 1886'. The date of electrification on this route is not established, so the horsecar-to-electric transition is drawn at the 1899 merger for want of anything better. All headways and speeds are estimates. Geometry is street-centreline routing rather than a traced alignment -- see geometry_quality.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. segments.note: The Albany Railway bought up its competitors in Albany, Troy, Watervliet and Cohoes, and in 1899 the Albany Railway, the Troy City Railway and the Watervliet Turnpike and Railroad merged as the United Traction Company. This was the trunk of the system and, for most people in most years, the way you got between Troy and Albany -- there was no through steam passenger service between the two cities on this bank. properties.geometry_source: Routed along present-day street centrelines from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass: a shortest path weighted to prefer Broadway and the river streets, from South Ferry Street in Albany north through Menands and Watervliet to Green Island, then across the Hudson into Troy. 576 points, 10.33 mi.
properties.geometry_quality: STREET-CENTRELINE ROUTING, not a traced track alignment. For a street railway this is close to the truth -- the cars ran in the roadway -- but which side of the street, the exact downtown terminal loops at each end, and the routing through Green Island and over the bridge are not verified against Sanborn or period track maps. Traced 8.71 mi from South Ferry to Green Island against the 7.5 miles of double track the Watervliet Turnpike and Railroad reported in 1886, so the drawn line is about 1.2 mi long over that stretch; the Green Island-Troy continuation adds 1.62 mi. No leg is a straight-line placeholder and there is no gap over 200 m.
